messages:
Maria (CS): Hey team, incoming escalation from ACME: their quantized endpoint (int8+calib) is now slower than the fp16 endpoint for multi-turn chat. p95 went from ~120ms to ~310ms after last calibration run. They see this mainly on longer prefixes (~800-1k tokens).
Samantha (Customer): Confirming. We repro'd on our side. Single request with ~900-token system prompt + 5-turn convo. fp16 p95 ~140ms, quant p95 ~320-400ms. Throughput also down. Nothing else changed on our end.
Cheng (Eng Runtime): Can you paste the request sizes + headers and whether you're using kv_cache:true? Also which model variant (name) are you hitting?
Samantha (Customer): model=redwood-v2-large-quant-calib-2026-03, kv_cache=true. Example payload: {"messages":[...], "max_tokens":256}
Maria (CS): Customer attached perf logs, they included per-request kernel decision events showing frequent fallback to "slow_quant_path" kernels and repeated kv cache re-allocs.
perf-bot: Attached flame timeline (short). GPU kernels show many small kernel launches with serialization spikes at ~0.9s intervals.
Cheng (Eng Runtime): Hmm. Two hypotheses: 1) calibration changed scale/zero-point causing extra dequant/requant around attention which pushes onto slow path. 2) Batching/kv_cache eviction heuristic is thrashing for long prefixes so we lose cache hits and fall back to full context recompute.
Julian (Eng ML): On the ML side we've seen calibration runs that increase per-layer scale variance. That can make the optimized int8 attention kernel pick a slower codegen path (safety checks). I'll pull the calib diffs.
Cheng (Eng Runtime): Can we get a repro script? If we can reproduce internally we can pin down kernel selector logs. Samantha, can you run this curl? 

``
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-large-quant-calib-2026-03","kv_cache":true,"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"x"}...],"max_tokens":256}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate
```

Cheng (Eng Runtime): Also please send the runtime config for batching thresholds and kv cache sizes.
Samantha (Customer): Running now, will paste logs.
Samantha (Customer): Logs: p95=338ms, kernel_selector: choose=slow_quant_path reason="high-scale-variance", kv_cache_evictions=12 per request
Alex (Oncall): I can repro quickly with a local microbench. Running microbench with long prefix and quant model. Early result: we hit slow_quant_path when layer_scale_stddev > 0.12. Also kv_cache hit rate drops below 40% when batch size > 4 and prefix > 700.
Cheng (Eng Runtime): Ok reproed. Profiler shows extra memcpy + dequant steps per layer: see snippet:

``
[profile] layer 23: dequant_kernel_ms=0.42, matmul_ms=1.8, reorder_ms=0.9
[profile] kernel_choice: fast_quant_path fail(safety_check), fallback=slow_quant_path
```

Cheng (Eng Runtime): Immediate mitigations:
- Customer-facing: temporarily route this customer's deployment to model variant redwood-v2-large-fp16 (routing override).
- Runtime: add kernel selector heuristic to prefer fp16 path when prefix_length > 512 and kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.5.
- Short-term: revert last calibration thresholds for the model in question while we investigate.
Julian (Eng ML): Reverting calibration will restore earlier scales; we'll prepare a rollback for that model artifact. Risk: potential small quality regression vs quant cost. Need CS approval.
Maria (CS): I'll propose routing to fp16 first (low-risk) and offer rollback if they accept. Draft comms:

"Hi Samantha — thanks for the report. We're temporarily routing your traffic to the fp16 variant while we investigate a calibration-induced performance regression. This should restore p95 to previous levels. We'll follow up with a root cause and timeline for a fix."

Cheng (Eng Runtime): Longer-term fix ideas:
- Make kernel selector aware of expected prefix length distribution per endpoint.
- Add a fast path when dequant ops would exceed X ms (avoid safety-heavy kernels under latency SLOs).
- Improve batching heuristics to avoid combining long prefix requests with user concurrency that triggers kv cache churn.
Alex (Oncall): Quick patch we can deploy today: bump per-endpoint batch_split_threshold to split long-prefix requests into their own smaller batch (config change, no code). That should increase kv_cache locality.
Samantha (Customer): Routing to fp16 would be fine for now. Can you confirm expected rollback time window?
Maria (CS): We'll route now and confirm. Estimated rollback of calibration in 1-2 hours once ML prepares artifact. Will update within 30m.
Cheng (Eng Runtime): Action items:
- Julian: prepare calibration rollback artifact and verification tests (owner: Julian).
- Alex: change batch_split_threshold on customer's endpoint and monitor p95 (owner: Alex).
- Maria: communicate routing override to customer and confirm acceptance (owner: Maria).
- Cheng: prototype kernel selector heuristic and open an RFC for evaluation (owner: Cheng).

(reacted :eyes:)
Alex (Oncall): Patch applied to customer's endpoint: batch_split_threshold -> 600 tokens. Monitoring shows p95 dropped to ~160ms after change (prelim).
Samantha (Customer): Confirmed, latency improved to ~155ms, thanks!
Maria (CS): Closing loop with customer, keeping on action list until calibration rollback tested.
Julian (Eng ML): Uploaded rollback artifact and unit perf tests. Starting QA.
Cheng (Eng Runtime): Will follow up with longer-term selector change. Thanks team.
